voter.py:214-228 `_merge_coverage_gap_decision` emits the string literal `"[LLM-Review: BLOCK — coverage-gap (merge-review)]"` directly, NOT via `_TAG_SUFFIXES`.

findings.finding: The eligibility parser is specified to rest on 'the `_TAG_SUFFIXES` vocabulary, test-asserted' AND to treat `merge-review` as a parseable coverage-gap sub-reason, but `_TAG_SUFFIXES` does not contain a `merge-review` key — that tag is emitted as a hardcoded literal outside the vocabulary.
findings.location: Approach → Step 3, 'Eligibility' bullet ('parse its first-line tag (the `_TAG_SUFFIXES` vocabulary, test-asserted) ... every coverage-gap sub-reason (including `merge-review` ...)')
scenarios: A contributor comments `recheck-review` on a merge change carrying `[LLM-Review: BLOCK — coverage-gap (merge-review)]`: a parser keyed only on `_TAG_SUFFIXES` fails to classify the tag and either falls through to the default-eligible branch by accident or misclassifies it, rather than via the asserted vocabulary path.
A test written to the plan's letter ('_TAG_SUFFIXES vocabulary, test-asserted' covers merge-review) cannot be satisfied because merge-review is not in that dict.
findings.suggested_fix: State that the parser must match the coverage-gap sub-reason token INSIDE `[LLM-Review: BLOCK — coverage-gap (<reason>)]` (a superset of `_TAG_SUFFIXES` that also includes the voter.py `merge-review` literal and tolerates the `(merge-change, N integrated commit(s))` suffix), and add `merge-review` to a single shared reason set (or centralize the merge tag through `_TAG_SUFFIXES`) so the 'test-asserted vocabulary' claim holds.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the eligibility parser to recognize the `merge-review` first-line tag as well (it lives in `voter.py::_merge_coverage_gap_decision`, not `_TAG_SUFFIXES`), or state that any `coverage-gap (...)` first-line tag is eligible so the vocabulary source is unambiguous.

findings.finding: The eligibility parser is specified against the `_TAG_SUFFIXES` vocabulary, but the plan lists `merge-review` as an eligible coverage-gap sub-reason — and `merge-review` is NOT a member of `_TAG_SUFFIXES`; it is a separately hardcoded tag string produced by `_merge_coverage_gap_decision` in voter.py. A parser keyed strictly to `_TAG_SUFFIXES` cannot classify a `merge-review` first-line tag, leaving that eligibility case under-specified or misrouted.
scenarios: A contributor comments `recheck-review` on a merge change whose current-revision tag is `merge-review`; the parser keyed to `_TAG_SUFFIXES` fails to recognize the tag and the eligibility decision is undefined.
findings.suggested_fix: Define eligibility as: refuse only a first-line tag matching `[LLM-Review: BLOCK — finding...]`; treat ANY other `[LLM-Review: BLOCK — coverage-gap (...)]` tag (including `merge-review`, which is not in `_TAG_SUFFIXES`) and PASS as eligible.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the finding-refusal to match the `finding` sub-reason regardless of the `(merge-change, N integrated commit(s))` suffix (match the tag STEM `BLOCK — finding`, not the exact bare string), and add a test asserting a merge-change finding tag is refused.
evidence: Plan: 'The ONLY ineligible state is a current-revision `[LLM-Review: BLOCK — finding]` tag'
adapter.py:82-84 `_message_tag` appends `(merge-change, N integrated commit(s))` INSIDE the tag suffix for merge changes
adapter.py:243 a merge change with blocking findings goes through `_block('finding', ...)`, so the finding tag on a merge change carries the merge-change suffix
findings.finding: The finding-refusal check is scoped to the exact tag `[LLM-Review: BLOCK — finding]`, but a real finding on a MERGE change renders with a suffix INSIDE the tag: `[LLM-Review: BLOCK — finding (merge-change, N integrated commit(s))]`. If the refusal match is exact/prefix-naive, a merge-change finding would not match and would be wrongly ACCEPTED for re-review — defeating the asserted security property on merge changes.
scenarios: A merge change carries a genuine `finding` BLOCK, so its tag is `[LLM-Review: BLOCK — finding (merge-change, 3 integrated commit(s))]`; an exact-match refusal on `[LLM-Review: BLOCK — finding]` does not fire and the contributor's `recheck-review` re-rolls the review on a real finding.
findings.suggested_fix: Classify by the tag's sub-reason token (`finding` vs `coverage-gap (...)`) rather than exact-string equality, so `[LLM-Review: BLOCK — finding (merge-change, ...)]` is still recognized as a finding and refused; assert this in AC2.

The vote-free capability is asserted but not verified.
findings.location: Approach §5 (Gerrit client) and Security property; Scope: gerrit_client.py
scenarios: A recheck-review refusal reply is posted via post_vote(value=0) and clears/re-registers the bot's prior LLM-Review vote, defeating the fail-closed gate the security property is meant to protect

findings.finding: The plan's finding-refusal rule ('refuse only a current-revision `[LLM-Review: BLOCK — finding]` tag') does not specify exact-vs-prefix tag matching, but on a MERGE change the finding tag renders with an in-tag suffix — `[LLM-Review: BLOCK — finding (merge-change, N integrated commit(s))]` — so an exact-equality match against the bare `BLOCK — finding` suffix would miss it and wrongly treat a real merge finding as eligible.
scenarios: A merge change carries a REAL finding tagged `[LLM-Review: BLOCK — finding (merge-change, 3 integrated commit(s))]`; a contributor comments `recheck-review`; an exact-string eligibility check on `BLOCK — finding` fails to match and re-runs the review — the exact self-approval dice-roll AC2 forbids.
findings.suggested_fix: State: refusal triggers when the first-line suffix STARTS WITH `BLOCK — finding` (covering both the bare and `(merge-change, ...)` variants); add a dedicated test for `[LLM-Review: BLOCK — finding (merge-change, 3 integrated commit(s))]` under AC2.

0347 runs automatic bounded escalation concurrently against the same review_attempts ledger
No mention of locking / atomicity for the reset-then-enqueue sequence
findings.finding: The plan resets the shared review_attempts ledger (reset_attempts DELETE) and then enqueues, but does not address concurrency on that shared state: two racing recheck-review comments, or a recheck-review racing with 0347's automatic escalation, could interleave reset and re-consumption. There is no stated atomicity (transaction/lock) or idempotency-under-retry guarantee for the reset+enqueue pair.
findings.location: Approach step 3 acceptance ('dedup.reset_attempts(...)') and step 4 (/rerun budget reset)
findings.suggested_fix: Note that the forced enqueue uses `_rebar_force` which already bypasses dedup and budget short-circuits, so a concurrent budget re-increment cannot block it; add a test asserting a double recheck-review (or recheck-review during escalation) yields at most one queued forced review.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify error handling for retrigger's new REST calls (message-fetch, reply-post) and the reset+enqueue sequence: on failure, define whether the path fails closed (no enqueue, no reset) and emits a greppable error marker.
evidence: Step 5 adds 'latest bot change message for a revision, and post-comment-without-vote' REST calls
Step 3 acceptance does reset_attempts then enqueue then post reply — no stated behavior if a call raises mid-sequence
'still fail-closed' is asserted for the force path but not for the new REST helpers
findings.finding: The new retrigger path makes Gerrit REST calls (fetch latest bot change message, post reply comment) and performs reset_attempts + enqueue, but the plan does not specify error handling if any of these fail — e.g. if the message-fetch fails, does the path fail-closed (no enqueue, no reset) or throw? The general 'fail-closed' claim is not tied to these specific new failure points.
findings.suggested_fix: State that any exception in eligibility fetch → skip (no enqueue, no reset) with a RETRIGGER_ERROR log; and that reset_attempts must occur only after eligibility passes, ideally after enqueue succeeds, to avoid resetting the budget without queuing a review.
